root_cause.text: An off-by-one bounds check in `drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c` let `hvc_iucv_get_private()` accept `num == hvc_iucv_devices`, which can index past the end of the fixed-size `hvc_iucv_table[8]` array when the device count is at its maximum.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)` to `if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)`, and the CVE description states that `MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES == 8`, `hvc_iucv_devices` can be `0..8`, and when `hvc_iucv_devices == 8` the old check allowed access to `hvc_iucv_table[8]` (out of bounds).

intent_record.what: The bounds check in hvc_iucv_get_private() was changed from `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)` to `if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)`, so the function now rejects indices equal to the device count as well as larger ones.
intent_record.how: This prevents an out-of-bounds access to `hvc_iucv_table[num]` when `num` is exactly the number of devices, ensuring only valid array indices from 0 to `hvc_iucv_devices - 1` are accepted.
